title: `this` and classes
summary: How this is decided by the call, how bind, call and arrow functions control it, and how classes, extends, super and static build objects.

concepts.title: Losing this: arrows, bind and call

misconceptions.description: Believes this inside a method is not the object it was called on: a global object, undefined, or an argument.
Believes this is fixed by where a function was written or by the first object that used it.
Believes this inside a function refers to that function.
Believes object state starts again from its first value on every call, or that bind works on a copy.
Believes bind calls the function immediately instead of returning a new function.
Believes a bound function takes this from the object it is called on.
Believes an arrow function gets its own this, like a regular function.
Believes all instances share one set of field values, or that fields live on the class.
Believes a class can be called like a function without new.
Believes an overriding method is ignored, or that the value returned by super.method() is dropped.
Believes a static method is available on instances, or cannot create instances of its own class.
Believes the parent constructor does not run when a subclass instance is created.
Takes the wrong run of a line that executes many times.
Reads the value a variable has at the end of the program for every earlier step.

conceptCard.title: this is the object before the dot
conceptCard.body: A method is a function stored on an object. When you call it as obj.method(), this inside it is obj. The same function called on another object sees that object instead.

lessons.title: Losing this: arrows, bind and call

conceptCard.title: Losing this, and fixing it
conceptCard.body: A method copied into a variable loses its object. call runs a function once with a chosen this. bind returns a new function with this fixed. An arrow function has no this of its own and uses the one around it.

conceptCard.title: Classes build objects
conceptCard.body: A class describes objects. new runs its constructor on a fresh object, and this inside the constructor is that object. Methods in the class see the instance they are called on as this.

conceptCard.title: extends, super and static
conceptCard.body: extends makes a subclass that inherits the parent's methods. A subclass constructor must call super() before using this. super.method() reaches the parent's version. static methods live on the class, not on instances.

A bound function ignores the object it is called on. Its this was fixed when bind ran.
You thought bind calls the function right away, which would make show a string. bind only returns a new function; it does not call it.

items.prompt: Which statement is true about this code?

options.text: The arrow function has no this of its own, so it uses the this of list.
options.feedback: Right. this.name inside the arrow is the same this as in list, which is club.

options.text: The callback gets its own this, so this.name is undefined.
options.feedback: A regular function would get its own this, but an arrow function does not. It uses the one around it.

options.text: this inside the arrow is the current member m.
options.feedback: The member is the parameter m. this is not a parameter, and it does not change with the element.

items.explanation: An arrow function takes this from the code around it. Inside list, this is club, so the arrow reads club.name for every member.
hints: Look at this.name on line 6, inside the arrow.
An arrow function does not create its own this.
Ask which this the code around the arrow has.

options.text: A static method belongs to the class and is not available on instances.
options.feedback: Right. Pair.twin works, but the instance p has no twin, so typeof gives undefined.

options.text: twin is copied to every instance, so p.twin is a function.

options.text: A static method cannot create instances of its own class.

items.prompt: Write bedArea(side). Class Square saves n; area() returns n * n. Subclass DoubleBed overrides area() to return twice the parent's, using super. Return new DoubleBed(side).area().
items.explanation: DoubleBed inherits the constructor from Square. Its area calls super.area() for the square and doubles it, so new DoubleBed(side).area() gives twice the square.
hints: Which class must you create with new at the end?
super.area() gives the parent's result inside the subclass method.
The subclass method needs the parent's result before it can change it.
